stories.headline: Odisha steps up evacuation plans as Cyclone Arnab approaches Andhra coast
stories.title: Odisha steps up evacuation plans as Cyclone Arnab approaches Andhra coast
stories.summary: State deploys disaster response teams and prepares shelters as IMD warns of extremely heavy rainfall in five districts from 28 October
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 2 independent source groups -> high confidence
article_sentences: A brewing cyclone in the Bay of Bengal, expected to intensify three times over as a very severe cyclone, threatens to unleash a spell of dangerous weather across the South Peninsula, with isolated extremely heavy rainfall exceeding 20 cm forecast over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal, and Kerala and Mahe.
Isolated to extremely heavy rainfall is likely also over Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam on Tuesday and Wednesday; and Telangana on Wednesday.
Heavy to very heavy rain (7-11 cm) is likely at isolated places over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal, Kerala and Mahe, and South Interior Karnataka.
Heavy rain at isolated places over Rayalaseema and Coastal Karnataka.
The bigger threat lies along the Andhra Pradesh coast, where the storm may make landfall by Wednesday.

Squally weather, gale-force winds and rough to very rough seas are forecast over the western and central Bay of Bengal from Tuesday, with impact spilling over to the Andhra Pradesh and adjoining Odisha coasts.

Sunday morning’s parent depression intensified into a deep depression and lay centred at over the same region about 420 km north-northwest of Sri Vijaya Puram (Andaman Islands), 870 km east-southeast of Vishakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 960 km east-southeast of Kakinada (Andhra Pradesh), 1060 km east- Southeast of Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and 1,130 km east of Bapatla (Andhra Pradesh).
It is very likely to move nearly southwest, and intensify further into a cyclonic storm over east-central and adjoining south-east Bay of Bengal early on Sunday morning.
Then it is very likely to move west-northwest over east-central and adjoining west-central Bay and intensify into a severe cyclone over west-central Bay by Tuesday morning.
Thereafter, it is very likely to move north-west, intensify further into a very severe cyclonic storm and reach west-central Bay near Andhra Pradesh coast around Wednesday morning.

It is very likely to cross Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam as a very severe cyclone with maximum sustained wind speed of 115-125 km/hr gusting to 140 km/hr by Tuesday midnight/Wednesday morning.
The IMD has also warned of dangerous sailing/fishing conditions over the Bay waters over next few days.

stories.headline: Cyclone threat prompts alert in Chittoor, Annamayya districts
stories.title: Cyclone threat prompts alert in Chittoor, Annamayya districts
stories.summary: District officials are ramping up precautions as forecasts warn of potential downpours, localised flooding, and crop damage ahead
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: With a brewing weather system over the Bay of Bengal threatening to turn into a cyclone, Chittoor and Annamayya districts are gearing up to counter the possible impact.
District officials are ramping up precautions as forecasts warn of potential downpours, localised flooding, and crop damage ahead.

Officials have flagged thunderstorms accompanied by lightning across Rayalaseema through October 28, though the exact severity for the twin districts hinges on how the system tracks and drops its rain.

Annamayya District Collector Nishant Kumar, addressing an urgent meeting in Madanapalle on Sunday, directed the departments to identify vulnerable spots like low-lying settlements, tanks, fragile roads, and power infrastructure.
He highlighted that emergency supplies, vehicles, and personnel should be kept ready in case of emergency.
The Collector said that departments, including Revenue, Police, Irrigation, Panchayat Raj, Health, and Fire Services, had been pulled into a joint disaster response framework.
In Chittoor, officials have been directed to stay on high alert through October 30, with a focus on Nagari, Vijayapuram, Nindra and Karveti Nagaram mandals.

stories.headline: Naidu puts officials on high alert as cyclone nears Andhra Pradesh coast
stories.title: Naidu puts officials on high alert as cyclone nears Andhra Pradesh coast
stories.summary: Ten NDRF and 11 SDRF teams kept ready; landfall likely between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam on October 28
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Sunday reviewed the State’s preparedness to deal with the impending cyclone, directing officials to remain on high alert and minimise disruption to people’s lives.
A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm and subsequently a severe cyclonic storm, according to the forecast presented at the review meeting.
Ten National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams and 11 State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) teams have been kept ready for relief and rescue operations.
Officials briefed the Chief Minister on evacuation plans, rehabilitation centres, food and drinking water supplies, medical assistance, power restoration and other precautionary measures.
The cyclone is likely to cross the coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam between the morning and afternoon of October 28.
Current projections indicate a possible landfall along the Konaseema-Yanam-Kakinada coastal belt.
The system is currently located about 850 km east-southeast of Visakhapatnam and 930 km from Kakinada.
It is likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm by the morning of October 26, a severe cyclonic storm by that night and a very severe cyclonic storm on October 27.
Wind speeds at landfall could reach 115-125 kmph, with gusts of up to 140 kmph in some areas.
Coastal districts are likely to experience strong winds from the morning of October 27.
Heavy to extremely heavy rainfall is forecast in North Andhra and the central coastal districts on October 27 and 28, with isolated places likely to receive exceptionally heavy rainfall.
Kakinada, Anakapalli, Visakhapatnam, Konaseema and East Godavari districts, along with other parts of North Andhra, are likely to be affected by strong winds and heavy rain.

stories.headline: Andhra Ministers put power utilities on alert ahead of cyclone; 25,000 poles kept ready
stories.title: Andhra Ministers put power utilities on alert ahead of cyclone; 25,000 poles kept ready
stories.summary: People can report power supply problems on helpline 1912 during the cyclone, officials say
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Andhra Pradesh Energy Minister Gottipati Ravi Kumar and Home Minister Vangalapudi Anitha on Sunday (October 25, 2026) alerted the Chairmen and Managing Directors (CMDs) of the power distribution companies (DISCOMs) and district officials to the likely impact of the cyclone brewing in the Bay of Bengal.
In a teleconference, Mr. Ravi Kumar and Ms. Anitha directed the officials to take precautionary measures in advance.
They advised the field staff to be on high alert for heavy rain and gales to meet any contingencies.
Power should be restored at the earliest if the power infrastructure is damaged, they said.
The Ministers also instructed the officials to try to prevent loss of life and mitigate property damage, and to remove dangerous hoardings and billboards.

In a post on X, Ms. Anitha asked fishermen not to venture into the sea and said the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) teams should be ready to move people to safe areas if necessary.
She asked people to stay away from beaches over the next five days and not to take selfies in hazardous areas.

Officials informed the Ministers that 25,000 poles and other essential materials had already been kept on standby and the DISCOMs were geared up to dispatch additional staff to areas expected to bear the brunt of the cyclone.
Cyclone warnings were being sent out regularly, and power supply problems could be reported on the helpline 1912, the officials added.
In a video conference with APGenco Managing Director S. Nagalakshmi, APTransco Joint Managing Director G. Surya Sai Praveenchand, DISCOM CMDs.

I. Prudhvi Tej, L. Siva Sankar and P. Pulla Reddy and other top officials of the power utilities, Special Chief Secretary (Energy) K. Vijayanand directed that emergency preparedness measures be taken urgently and steps initiated to safeguard critical power supply infrastructure.

He instructed the CMDs and Directors to camp in the vulnerable areas from October 26 until the threat subsided and normal conditions were restored, and said that public safety and grid security must remain the foremost priorities.

stories.headline: 100 shelters ready, schools shut, ports on alert: How Odisha, Tamil Nadu and Andhra are bracing for October 28 cyclone
stories.title: 100 shelters ready, schools shut, ports on alert: How Odisha, Tamil Nadu and Andhra are bracing for October 28 cyclone
stories.summary: The weather system developed from a low-pressure area over the east-central and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal and intensified into a depression on October 24.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: If the system intensifies into a cyclonic storm, it will be named Arnab.
Bangladesh contributed the name, which means “ocean” in Bengali, to the regional cyclone naming list maintained by the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) and the IMD.
The weather system developed from a low-pressure area over the east-central and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal and intensified into a depression on October 24.
The IMD has forecast that it will move west-northwestwards, strengthen into a deep depression and then a cyclonic storm before approaching the Andhra Pradesh coast.
IMD Director General Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said the system had wind speeds of around 35-45 kmph, gusting to 55 kmph, at the time of his statement on Friday.
At landfall, winds could reach 115-125 kmph, with gusts of up to 140 kmph.
Cyclone warning signals have been hoisted at nine ports, including Chennai, Nagapattinam, Cuddalore, Karaikal, Pamban and Thoothukudi.
Puducherry and parts of Tamil Nadu have also been seeing continuous rainfall, with waterlogging reported in parts of Puducherry, including Coast Road, Krishna Nagar and Laspet Sarum.
Odisha has stepped up preparations as southern and coastal districts are likely to face heavy rain and strong winds.
Schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres will remain closed in Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri on October 28 and 29.
The state has mobilised around 60 ODRAF teams, 17 NDRF teams and 225 Fire Services teams.
The IMD has issued a red warning for the five districts for October 28, with very heavy rainfall and isolated extremely heavy rain exceeding 20 cm.

stories.headline: Using terrorism as instrument of statecraft simply unacceptable: Jaishankar
stories.title: Using terrorism as instrument of statecraft simply unacceptable: Jaishankar
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 25: The use of terrorism as an "instrument of statecraft" is simply unacceptable, and it can never be justified or rationalised, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said on Sunday and flagged that it continues because "not all states really display zero tolerance" for the menace. Despite history holding so many lessons on it, "some still allow political calculations to take precedence", he said in his address at an event here without naming any country. At an event held here to mark the 75th anniversary of Chinmaya Mission, the minister underlined the importance of peace, especially amid the ongoing conflicts in the world, and cautioned that "war anywhere threatens peace everywhere". He cited the two major conflicts going on in the world, in Ukraine and in West Asia, and said societies and economies and people far away who have little say in the matter are actually "paying the cost". "We cannot remain helpless spectators. India expresses global sentiment when we urge that dialogue and diplomacy are the only solution," the EAM said. The minister underlined that India is making efforts towards peace building and is open to working with other partners to that end. "Terrorism is another deadly threat to peace. Its usage as an instrument of statecraft is simply unacceptable. It can never be justified. It can never be rationalised. Yet it continues because not all states really display zero tolerance. Despite history holding so many lessons, some still allow political calculations to take precedence," Jaishankar said. The world must, therefore, develop sharper awareness about this common threat, and it must come together with stronger resolve and counter terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, he said. Jaishankar delivered the address in the presence of UN Resident Coordinator in India, Stefan Priesner, who also shared the dais with him. The external affairs minister underlined that progress and prosperity are the flip side of conflicts and violence and are equally indivisible. "The world cannot advance half prosperous and half denied. In an era of intricate supply chains, of globalised markets, and of common resources, this is simply a prescription for continuous instability," he cautioned. Jaishankar reiterated that the Global South today faces a '4F' crisis -- of finance, fuel, food and fertiliser and said the Global North must realise that it has "equal stakes" in finding solutions. "The international economy must be urgently derisked and nations provided with more diversified options. Market distortions through constriction and chokepoints only add to suffering. A genuine dialogue in this regard is overdue," the minister said. In his address, he also said the United Nations must show leadership, and "not be a spectator" to global crises, while asserting that the case for "reformed multilateralism" gets stronger by the day. "We know we live in an imperfect world. But we all continuously strive towards greater perfection," Jaishankar said. As far as the UN is concerned, that means "recognising its shortcomings and limitations" and seeking "improvement," the minister added. "The case for reformed multilateralism gets stronger by the day. Large parts of the world cannot be left out from decision-making. The UN must show leadership, not be a spectator to global crisis," Jaishankar said. The Union minister also emphasised that people have witnessed perpetual arguments between those who stress competitiveness and others who see a virtue in cooperation. "These may be individual or even societal predicaments, but on the global stage, they translate into how nations behave with one another," he said. On the role of evolving technology, especially artificial intelligence (AI) in reshaping the world, Jaishankar said that humankind now really stands at the crossroads. "AI promises to be the mother of all change. But something so sweeping, something so consequential, it cannot be left in the hands of just a few. That would go counter to the trends of freedom and democratisation that the world has seen over the last 80 years," he said. For this reason, India is a strong advocate of a "responsible, inclusive, and human-centric approach", he said. That is a recognition of AI's universal applicability and of the need to develop a wider perspective, the EAM added. Emphasising India's development cooperation with a large number of countries, and helping them out in times of need and crises, he said, for India, the ethos of "Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam is practised, it is not merely preached".
